title: Cracking into RACS - I. Measuring the cosmic dipole in the RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 radio surveys with simulation-based inference
summary: Simulation-based inference applied to two Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey bands found radio-galaxy count dipoles inconsistent with the cosmic microwave background kinematic dipole. The low-band dipole agreed in direction and had about four times the expected amplitude. The mid-band dipole was offset in direction and had about five times the expected amplitude. Warmer antennas were associated with lower reported flux densities. The inference depends on survey modeling and simulations.
ai_technology: A neural network in a simulation-based inference pipeline learned the likelihood function from simulated survey data, including a model of antenna-temperature effects on flux density.
organization: Australian National University; University of Western Australia

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: The study used a neural-network likelihood trained on simulations, with coverage and posterior checks across survey bands.
evidence.unknown: Inference depends on simulation fidelity, survey calibration and foreground/systematic modeling; it does not establish the cause of the dipole discrepancy.
